title: Talent Ecosystem Handbook and Onboarding Platform — 2029
author: Marisol Ortega
content:
Overview

Purpose
This handbook describes Redwood’s integrated talent ecosystem: how we welcome new hires, align role expectations and career ladders, operate core benefits and perks programs, and provision the internal tools that enable fast impact. It is intended for new hires, managers, people-ops partners, and hiring stakeholders.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors on 6+ month engagements, and interns converting to FTE.
- Covers the end-to-end experience from offer acceptance through the first 12 months, plus promotion and internal mobility processes.

How this document is organized
1) Our approach and principles
2) Role & career ladder summaries and level expectations
3) Hiring and onboarding flows (checklists and SLAs)
4) Benefits, perks and flexibility programs summary
5) Internal tools, provisioning matrix and access SLAs
6) First-90 / first-year milestone templates
7) Promotion, feedback, and mobility procedures
8) Governance, owners and review cadence

1) Principles of Redwood’s talent ecosystem
- Engineer- and manager-first: minimize friction for making an impact in product and infra roles.
- Predictable ramp: clear milestones and artifacts to assess progress.
- Portable skill signals: levels, competencies, and badges should be interpretable across teams.
- Human-centered benefits: support flexibility, caregiver needs, mental health, and professional growth.
- Security-by-default: tool access follows least privilege with documented exceptions.

2) Roles and Career Ladders (summary)
This section provides a high-level synopsis of level expectations. Detailed competency matrices are stored in the career-lattice page (see related_pages).

- IC Track (IC3 — IC7+)
  - IC3: Entry/early contributor. Focus: deliver single-scope features, accept feedback, document work.
  - IC4: Solid contributor. Focus: owning features, basic design, mentoring interns.
  - IC5: Senior contributor. Focus: cross-team projects, shaping technical direction, measurable impact.
  - IC6: Staff-equivalent. Focus: technical leadership, architecture ownership, influencing across orgs.
  - IC7+: Principal/Distinguished. Focus: company-level strategy, external representation, major cross-product initiatives.

- Manager Track (M1 — M3+)
  - M1 (Manager): Leads a team of ~3–7, performance and delivery ownership, coaching.
  - M2 (Senior Manager): Manages managers or larger teams, cross-team coordination, hiring plans.
  - M3+: Director-level. Strategy, org design, and multi-quarter planning.

Expectations and artifacts
- Every level has 3 core artifacts: 1) role expectations doc, 2) 90-day plan template, 3) impact portfolio sample. Managers must maintain a calibrated hiring rubric for their team.

3) Hiring & Onboarding: Flow, owners, and SLAs
Summary flow (offer -> pre-boarding -> week 0 -> week 1 -> 30/60/90 reviews):
1. Offer accepted (owner: recruiting) — start pre-boarding checklist within 24 hours.
2. Pre-boarding (owner: people-ops) — equipment, accounts, initial 1:1 with manager scheduled. SLA: equipment order placed within 48 hours, accounts provisioning request submitted same day.
3. Day 0 (welcome) — team intro, role expectations, first-week schedule, badge/office access.
4. Week 1 — systems training, codebase orientation, security brief, first small deliverable assigned.
5. Week 2–4 — onboarding tasks + buddy check-ins; manager reviews early ramp.
6. 30/60/90 checkpoints — documented in Lattice/HRIS and archived to the employee file.

Hiring and onboarding checklists (minimal, manager + people-ops responsibilities)
- People-ops pre-boarding checklist:
  - Confirm start date and equipment needs.
  - Open accounts: email, SSO, VPN, identity provider.
  - Add to payroll/benefits enrollment queue.
  - Assign onboarding buddy and announce in team channel.
- Manager checklist:
  - Create first-week plan and 90-day milestones.
  - Schedule role-specific training and product walkthroughs.
  - Assign first small ticket and pair programming session.
  - Complete Level expectations alignment meeting within 2 weeks.

Provisioning SLAs and escalation
- Standard accounts provisioned within 2 business days of pre-boarding submission.
- Elevated access (production, secret stores) requires explicit approval and typically completes within 5 business days after manager justification and security review.
- Escalation path: people-ops -> security engineering -> team lead. Response SLA: initial reply within 4 business hours during business days.

4) Benefits & Perks (concise summary)
- Health and wellness: comprehensive medical/dental/vision plans with company contribution; mental health EAP and unlimited therapy stipend (up to $1,200/year).
- Flexible leave: 18 weeks primary caregiver leave (paid), 8 weeks secondary caregiver leave, 4-week paid sabbatical after 5 years.
- Flexible returnship and reboarding: 12-month flexible returnship program for caregivers and phased reboarding allowances.
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual L&D stipend + dedicated learning weeks and internal mentorship credits.
- Home office stipend: $600 initial, $150 annual refresh.
- Commuter & travel: market-specific commuter benefits + monthly coworking credits for distributed employees.

Unique programs (high-level)
- Impact Fellowship: 6‑month internal rotation with executive sponsorship for high-potential ICs.
- Manager-in-Residence: 3-month fast-path for ICs transitioning to first-time managers with cohort-based training.

5) Internal Tools and Provisioning Matrix
This table captures the minimum toolset provided by default by role. Managers may request additional tooling via the provisioning portal (link in Related Pages).

| Role / Persona           | Default Tools Provisioned                            | SLA (standard) | Provisioning Owner |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|----------------|--------------------|
| Engineer (IC3–IC5)      | GitHub, CI runner, Slack, SSO, Jira, Dev VPN         | 2 business days| people-ops / infra |
| Senior Engineer (IC5+)  | Above + staging infra access, profiling tools        | 3 business days| infra + people-ops |
| Product / PM            | Jira, Confluence, Slack, Analytics dashboards        | 2 business days| people-ops         |
| Security / Compliance   | Above + KMS read access (role-based)                 | 5 business days| security eng.      |
| Contractor (<6mo)       | Limited GitHub, Slack guest, email, Jira limited     | 2 business days| people-ops         |

Note: Production secrets access always requires a manager justification ticket and security approval.

Tooling standards and how-tos (short list)
- GitHub: repo naming conventions, protected branches and PR template.
- CI/CD: use the standardized pipeline templates in repos/template-ci.
- Observability: request org-level Grafana dashboards through infra runbook.
- Local dev: standard dev container definitions live in infra/devcontainer/.

6) First-90 / First-Year milestone templates (to be completed jointly by manager and hire)
- 0–30 days:
  - Complete secure onboarding and required compliance trainings.
  - Ship a small, reviewer-assigned change to mainline.
  - Attend three product area deep-dive sessions.
- 30–60 days:
  - Deliver a scoped feature or meaningful bugfix end-to-end.
  - Present a learning summary to the team.
  - Establish recurring 1:1s and career checkpoints.
- 60–90 days:
  - Take owner-level responsibility for a component or cross-team task.
  - Capture an impact portfolio artifact (PR, doc, dashboard) for performance calibration.
- First year outcomes (concise): achieve expected ramp level, complete L&D plan, and identify a growth pathway (technical leadership, IC craft, or people management).

7) Promotion, Calibration, and Internal Mobility
Promotion cadence and eligibility
- Promotion considerations: impact volume, scope growth, leadership influence, and competency alignment with the target level.
- Typical eligibility windows: 9–18 months between promotions at earlier levels; longer for senior staff roles.

Promotion process (high level)
1. Candidate and manager prepare promotion packet (impact portfolio, feedback, rubric mapping).
2. Manager submits packet to calibration committee and schedules calibration meeting.
3. Committee review includes cross-functional peers and PeopleOps representative.
4. Decision and feedback are returned to the manager within 10 business days.

Internal mobility and rotations
- Apply via internal roles board. Hiring manager must coordinate with current manager and PeopleOps for a transition plan.
- Short-term rotations (≤6 months) use the Impact Fellowship pathway or manager-approved secondments.

8) Governance, Owners and Review Cadence
- Document owner: people-ops (Marisol Ortega).
- Review cadence: full review annually in January; tactical updates as needed quarterly.
- Escalation and exception authority: VP People & Ops for benefits exceptions; Security for elevated access exceptions.
